verdict.rationale: Jules is itself an AI coding agent, and its docs describe the delegation loop end to end: submit a task (including via a GitHub 'jules' label), review and approve its plan, get notified, then review diffs and PRs. Hands-on users confirm they delegate tasks and get back usable PRs. Missing for 10: dependable completion on complex tasks, since users report timeouts and endless loops with no stop button.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Once you submit a task, Jules will generate a plan. You can review and approve it before any code changes are made.
Use the "jules" label in an issue to assign a task directly in GitHub.
You’ll be notified when the task completes or needs your input.
Jules creates a PR of the changes.
By the time I get home in the evening I've got a few PRs to review.
